source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Europa pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: JPL parent-relative satellite orbit plus VSOP87 Jupiter position, with IAU/WGCCRE rotation
provenance.qualification: Computed Europa Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: USGS Voyager/Galileo mosaic. Source resolution varies from about 200 m to 20 km per pixel. Gray grid marks documented no-data and its resampled boundary. Original image shading remains; globe lighting is approximate.
controls.summary: Source detail ranges from 200 m to 20 km per pixel. Photographed shadows remain; the gray grid marks missing imagery.
controls.title: Global image mosaic

controls.label: Enhanced color
controls.description: Galileo enhanced color: 756 nm → red, 559 nm → green, 404 nm → blue, at 1.4–1.6 km per pixel. Color covers part of the surface. A correction for each observation reduces broad photographed shading; oblique views retain observed monochrome. Overall brightness is matched to the monochrome base, preserving color ratios. Photographed shadows and seams can remain; added globe lighting is approximate. Gray grid marks gaps in both sources.
controls.summary: Enhanced colors are combined with monochrome detail. Where color is unavailable, gray imagery remains; the grid marks gaps in both.
controls.title: SSI enhanced-color mosaic

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Agenor Linea only, near 142°E and 44°S. Colors encode the released local stereo heights in meters; their relative datum is not a global reference level. Effective detail is about 3 km. Fixed northwest cartographic relief shows slopes; it is not part of the numeric scale. Gray grid preserves the DTM’s finite/no-data footprint. The archive’s duplicated, cubic-resampled quality products are excluded; colors imply no quality class or pointwise accuracy.

facts.label: Source precision
facts.value: Nominal 52 m; approximately 100 m empirical estimate, not a pointwise error bound

controls.title: Agenor Linea stereo terrain model

controls.label: Geology
controls.description: USGS interpreted regional plains, bands, chaos terrains and crater deposits (2024; 1:15,000,000). Colors identify map units, not measured surface color. Gray grid marks no-data polygons. Fine line and point features are not represented by this polygon view.
controls.title: USGS global geology (2024 SIM 3513)

controls.label: Infrared
controls.description: Galileo NIMS observations assign red, green and blue to 1.50, 1.34 and 0.73–0.74 µm, following the archive guide. This false-color view shows spectral differences, not natural color or mineral abundance. The observations have Minnaert photometric correction; resolution, residual brightness and seams vary. Fixed channel stretches clip extreme values. Gray grid marks areas lacking a valid sample in any selected band.
controls.title: Galileo NIMS spectral color
